examples.claim: Waste under 4%; existing systems waste 60-80%; up to 24x throughput vs HF Transformers without model changes
examples.source: vLLM blog: 'a mere waste of under 4%'; 'existing systems waste 60% – 80% of memory due to fragmentation and over-reservation'; 'up to 24x higher throughput than HuggingFace Transformers, without requiring any model architecture changes'

examples.claim: Block size 4, 7-token prompt: logical 0,1 -> physical 7,1 (4/4, 3/4); decode 1 fills block 1; decode 2 allocates physical block 3
examples.source: paper §4.3: 'maps the first 2 logical KV blocks (0 and 1) to 2 physical KV blocks (7 and 1) ... first 4 tokens in logical block 0 and the following 3 tokens in logical block 1 ... allocates a new physical block (physical block 3)'

examples.claim: Parallel sampling: both sequences' logical blocks 0 and 1 map to physical 7 and 1, reference counts both 2
examples.source: paper §4.4: 'the logical block 0 and 1 of both sequences are mapped to physical blocks 7 and 1 ... the reference counts for physical blocks 7 and 1 are both 2'

examples.claim: Beam k=4: each candidate used 4 full blocks, all share block 0, candidate 3 diverges from the second block, 0-2 share first 3 blocks
examples.source: paper §4.4: 'with k = 4 ... each candidate sequence has used 4 full logical blocks. All beam candidates share the first block 0 ... Candidate 3 digresses from others from the second block. Candidates 0-2 share the first 3 blocks'

examples.claim: --max-num-batched-tokens / --max-num-seqs limit tokens / sequences per iteration; defaults mainly for testing, set in EngineArgs.create_engine_config; --max-num-batched-tokens accepts 1k/1K/25.6k
examples.source: vllm/config/scheduler.py docstrings ('The default value here is mainly for convenience when testing. In real usage, this should be set in EngineArgs.create_engine_config'); arg_utils.py human_readable_int_args includes 'max_num_batched_tokens'

examples.claim: Async scheduling is disabled with --no-async-scheduling and avoids GPU utilization gaps
examples.source: scheduler.py: 'async_scheduling: bool | None ... If set to False, disable async scheduling. Async scheduling helps to avoid gaps in GPU utilization'; arg_utils.py uses argparse.BooleanOptionalAction for bool fields

examples.claim: Swap copies blocks to CPU and back, cost set by CPU-GPU bandwidth, worse with small blocks; recompute is constant across block sizes
examples.source: paper §4.5/§7.3: 'we copy evicted blocks to the CPU memory'; 'swapping incurs excessive overhead with small block sizes ... limits the effective PCIe bandwidth ... the overhead of recomputation remains constant across different block sizes'

examples.claim: ROCm quickstart wheel supports Python 3.12, ROCm 7.0, glibc >= 2.35; GPU page requires ROCm 6.3+, MI350 7.0+
examples.source: quickstart.md AMD tab: 'It currently supports Python 3.12, ROCm 7.0 and glibc >= 2.35'; gpu.rocm.inc.md: 'ROCm 6.3 or above - MI350 requires ROCm 7.0 or above' (note: the same page now says pre-built wheels are for ROCm 10.0)

examples.claim: Server applies generation_config.json by default; --generation-config vllm disables it
examples.source: quickstart.md: 'By default, the server applies generation_config.json ... To disable this behavior, please pass --generation-config vllm'

examples.claim: 28,672 B/token, 18 GiB -> ~674,000 tokens -> ~164 concurrent 4,096-token requests; 1-byte KV dtype doubles tokens
examples.source: Arithmetic check: 2*28*2*128*2 = 28,672; 18*2^30/28,672 = 674,133; /4096 = 164.6 (labelled as an assumed example)

examples.claim: Issue #7155 (2024) proposed limiting allocation by max_model_len and was auto-closed as not planned later that year
examples.source: GitHub API: state CLOSED, stateReason NOT_PLANNED, closedAt 2024-12-04

examples.claim: The server passes 'the same arguments' as the LLM(max_model_len=4096, ...) block via --max-model-len 4k
examples.source: vllm/config/model.py: 'supports k/m/g/K/M/G in human-readable format ... 1k -> 1000, 1K -> 1024'; 4k = 4,000, so the flag form should be 4K or 4096

examples.claim: 2-4x throughput over FasterTransformer and Orca without accuracy loss; up to 22x higher request rate vs FasterTransformer on ShareGPT
examples.source: paper §1: 'improves the LLM serving throughput by 2-4× ... without affecting the model accuracy at all'; §6.2: 'Compared to FasterTransformer, vLLM can sustain up to 22× higher request rates'

examples.claim: FastChat-vLLM handled up to 5x more traffic; average 30K, peak 60K requests daily
examples.source: vLLM blog: 'support the growing demands (up to 5x more traffic)'; 'an average of 30K requests daily and a peak of 60K' (the post calls them '처리량', but they are request counts)

examples.claim: '같은 글' (Deploybase) published an internal benchmark: Llama 70B 4-bit GPTQ on 8x H200, Triton-TRT 5210, SGLang 4880, vLLM 4250, TGI 3120 tok/s
